title: fix(post): stop between setups by default (#1532)
body:
## What changed

A two-setup document posted as one program ran from Setup 1's last cut straight into Setup 2's first, on a part still clamped for Setup 1. A new document post option, **Between setups**, decides what posts at a setup change:

| Word | Label | Posts |
|---|---|---|
| `pause` (default) | Pause (M0) | a program stop after each setup's last operation, with a comment naming the next setup |
| `optional-stop` | Optional stop (M1) | the same, as an optional stop |
| `continue` | Run straight on | the old program |
| `file-per-setup` | One file per setup | one whole program per setup (the multi-file post) |

- `crates/app/src/posting_setup_change.rs` (new): folds the stop into the setup's last operation's after-action, so each dialect writes it where it writes an operator's own stop (spindle and coolant off), and adds `PARAM SetupChange "<next setup>"` for the comment. Independent of "Skip pauses and homes" (a proven program still needs the part turned over). A Go home at the change is refused by name; an operation's own M0 there merges into the one stop. Per mount (one file: one machine, and one post unless an explicit script posts them all): a mount's last operation gets no stop, so two setups on different posts still post one clean file each.
- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: at a setup-change stop, `G91 G28 Z0`, `G90`, `(SETUP CHANGE - NEXT: <setup>)`, then M0/M1.
- `assets/posts/tormach.cps`: now declares `afterModes` (it never read stops before, so a stop on Tormach was refused); writes `G53 G0 Z..`, `(MSG, SETUP CHANGE - NEXT: <setup>)`, M0/M1; a Go home is refused there (the G30 spot is the operator's preset).
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`: a script without `afterModes` is refused at a setup change by name (once, not doubled by the generic after-operation refusal).
- One file per setup splits the mounts per setup (`post_mounts`); the one-file post refuses such a program by name.
- Project key `post_options.between_setups` (only written off default; an unknown word refuses to open); setup-owned post options carry it and are compared for it by the program-level check.
- UI: a "Between setups" combo box under the post options, through `SetPostOptions`.
- MCP: `post` takes an optional `between_setups` word, applied first through the undoable `SetPostOptions` (or `SetSetupPostOptions` when the active setup owns its options); the camcraft-mcp skill row says so.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1532-setup-boundary-stop.md`.

Process change: yes (the camcraft-mcp skill's `post` row).

## Goldens changed

- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/live_then_stop.refusal`: the "does not declare afterModes" warning is gone, because tormach.cps now reads after-actions (3 warnings instead of 4; the program is still refused).

No NC golden changed.

## How tested

Pinning tests, `crates/app/tests/between_setups.rs`:
- `the_default_pauses_between_setups_on_fanuc_with_a_comment_naming_the_next`
- `the_default_pauses_between_setups_on_tormach_and_an_optional_stop_writes_m1`
- `run_straight_on_is_the_old_program_and_is_undoable`
- `one_file_per_setup_writes_two_whole_programs`
- `a_post_that_cannot_stop_is_refused_by_name_at_the_setup_change`
- `a_go_home_at_the_setup_change_is_refused_by_name`
- `the_choice_round_trips_and_the_default_writes_no_key`
- `the_mcp_post_tool_takes_the_choice_through_the_undoable_command`

Updated: `setup_post_options::a_setup_that_skips_posts_without_its_stops_while_the_other_follows_the_document` (now sets Run straight on, since its two setups would otherwise pause between them).
- `program_entry::pause_and_home_entries_post_goldens_and_tormach_refuses_by_name`: Tormach now reads after-actions, so its Go home refusal is tormach.cps's own ("a trip home is asked after the operation in operation <name> ...") instead of the engine's afterModes refusal.
- `setup_mount::two_setups_on_different_posts_post_one_file_each` unchanged; it caught the first cut of the fold placing the stop per machine (fixed in the second commit).

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`): green on head 6d171bf07 (post ok 35s, app ok 914s, ui ok 64s; logs gate-logs/quick-20261114-091458). The previous run, on 51c1611f9, failed program_entry and setup_mount; both are fixed in the second commit. Clippy on camcraft-app, camcraft-post, camcraft-ui: clean (`-D warnings`).

## Not exercised

- No real control ran the output: the Fanuc and PathPilot programs are checked by text only.
- The other afterModes dialects (Haas, Mazak, Sinumerik, Heidenhain, ...) write the stop without the Z lift and the comment: follow-up #1647.
- The UI combo box was not clicked in the running app (not launched).
- The script `post` verb takes no between_setups argument (MCP and UI do).

Changelog: A program that runs from one setup into the next now stops there by default (M0 with a comment naming the next setup); "Between setups" in the post options chooses an optional stop, running straight on, or one file per setup (#1532, PR #1650)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1532

title: fix(2d): judge a part-source cross drill against the setup's other parts
body:
**Stacked on #1640** - review only after da340c0f; merge #1615, #1622, #1634, #1640 first. (Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch based on #1640's head da340c0f.)

## What changed

#1621's neighbour law (`keep_law::neighbour_parts`) judged a part-source op against the setup's OTHER parts only when `depth_law_of` was not `None`. A Drill with cross holes reads `None` (its part law is the radial `cross_part`), so its neighbour set was empty, and the program sim does not judge a posed (radial) chain.

- `keep_law::kept_models` now includes a part-source cross drill (`is_cross_drill`): the setup's parts but the source, fixtures and a stock-only model left out.
- `cross_spindle::Solids` gains `neighbours`. After the source's own `cross_part::part_clear`, the new `cross_part::neighbours_clear` sweeps the finished chain (drill, shank, holder, rapids, posed along each move's axis) against those parts with **no hole wall excused**, on and off the work offset, and refuses by name.
- A stock-source cross drill passes no neighbours (#1635 already judges every part in its stock).

## Readings (reproduced first, on da340c0f)

Mill-turn bench, B = the #117 r10 punched bar with its r2 cross hole modelled (legal for B), A = a box; r20 bar and 40 x 40 box stocks, aligned and turned a quarter about Z; op on source "B".

| case | before (all four stocks) | now |
|---|---|---|
| A x [12, 18] across the drill's line, no hole in A | generates clean, **posts** | refused: "cross hole at (10, 0, 0) along (-1, 0, 0) cuts into a neighbouring part: another part the setup holds stands in the drill's line or its approach ..."; nothing written |
| A outside the raw bar, in the approach only | - | refused by name, aligned and turned |
| A a tube whose r3 32-gon bore sits on the line (B's r3 hole at size) | - | refused (a neighbour's wall is never excused) |
| A on B's far side, or 2 mm over the drill | posts | posts |

So it was a real P1: a gouge of part A posted unjudged on both stocks.

## How tested

Pins in `crates/app/tests/cross_drill_neighbours.rs`:
- `a_cross_drill_on_b_into_part_a_is_refused_by_name_on_both_stocks`
- `a_cross_drill_whose_approach_crosses_part_a_is_refused_on_both_stocks`
- `a_neighbours_round_hole_on_the_line_is_not_excused`
- `a_cross_drill_on_b_clear_of_part_a_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `over_mcp_a_part_source_cross_drill_answers_for_the_neighbour_the_same` (MCP parity: `add_operation` with `"source": "B"`)

Mutations (each alone, then reverted; `stock_source_cross_drill.rs` also run):

| mutation | red |
|---|---|
| M1 cross drill out of `kept_models` (the old predicate) | into, approach, tube, MCP |
| M2 `neighbours_clear` not called | into, approach, tube, MCP |
| M3 source's hole walls excused on the neighbours | tube |
| M4 2D tail's neighbour law skipped for a cross drill | none - so no guard was added; the tail's law stays on as a second net |
| M5 part-source arm passes no neighbours | into, approach, tube, MCP |

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on bf2dcaa7 (sim, motion, app, ui suites; 22.5 min, 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

A plain lathe holding two parts; the 3+2 frame arm (a cross drill is lathe / mill-turn work); MCP on a turned stock (`set_stock` takes no rotation).

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1641-cross-drill-neighbours.md`.

Changelog: A part-source cross drill whose drill or approach enters another part in the setup is refused by name instead of posting (#1641)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1641

title: fix(2d): judge the parts beside an op's source again live at the post
body:
Stacked on #1622 (branch `issue/1607-stock-source-law`; the `keep_law::parts_in_stock` / `neighbour_parts` code exists only there). Fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

Since #1603 / #1607 / #1621 an operation is judged against parts BESIDE its source, but those parts are not in its stamp. A part moved into the cut, added, or un-tagged as a fixture after a clean generation left the op `Ok`. On a turned stock (the program sim refuses to judge) the post read the cached clean verdict and posted into the part.

**Decision: option (c), no stamp term** (`docs/decisions/1628-kept-parts-live-judge.md`). When the program sim cannot judge, the post gate (`posting_sim`, not-judged arm) judges the parts again live:
- `operation::kept_rejudge::moved_part_problem` runs on each program op whose cached verdict is clean and whose kept part set is non-empty. It collects the op's job again and re-runs, on the cached path, the laws generation ran: the solid law (`contain_into`, `DepthLaw::Keep`), or the budgeted mark law for a stock-source Engrave/Trace. It uses the same cutter, stock to leave, excess and 3+2 frame, and the tap's core acquittal. It checks one kept part at a time, as each part stands now.
- A cut is refused by name: `stock sim did not judge this program: ... - and N1 now cuts part 'other' (move 328 cuts past the finish surface) - a part moved, added or no longer workholding since it was generated; regenerate it`.
- An op whose cached warnings already block is skipped, so it is still refused by its own findings, by name.
- On an aligned stock nothing changes: the sim already judges every part live.
- `generate::stock_to_leave_of`: the stock-to-leave table is moved out of `run_job_arms` unchanged, so both judges read one number. `contain_into` is now `pub(super)`. `keep_law::kept_parts_named` gives the kept set one mesh per model, by name.

Why not (a), the stamp term: it breaks the contracts the issue lists. With (c) they all pass unchanged on this branch: `fixtures::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath`, `operations::a_frommodel_stock_survives_its_source_being_deleted`, `operations::a_model_update_does_not_touch_a_box_stock`, `fidelity_copies` (both tests), and `stock_source_verdict`. All of these were in the quick gate.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/kept_parts_live.rs`, all on a turned stock)
- `a_neighbour_moved_into_a_part_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_is_refused_by_name`: a Trace on B is generated clean, then A is moved into its flank. The op stays Ok, and the post is refused naming `N1` and `other`. With A moved away again, the program posts.
- `a_part_added_into_a_stock_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_is_refused_by_name`: a stock-source Slot in the pocket is generated clean, then a boss is added under it. The op stays Ok, and the post is refused naming `S1` and `boss`.
- `a_fixture_untagged_then_moved_into_a_part_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_is_refused_by_name`: the clamp is tagged, then untagged. The op stays Ok (the M2.3 law) and the program posts. The clamp is then moved into the cut and the post is refused naming `clamp`.
- `a_part_moved_into_a_stock_source_cut_on_a_turned_stock_never_posts`: moving the part under a stock-source op already stales it (another stamp input), so the post is refused with "regenerate".

## Mutation checks (each line reverted, the test run red, then restored and touched)
1. The gate's `.or_else(|| kept_moved(..))` replaced with nothing: the 3 `kept_parts_live` refusal tests go red.
2. The refusal in `moved_part_problem` (`if let Some(w) = ... find(blocks_post)`) never taken: the same 3 go red.
3. The convicted-op skip in `kept_moved` deleted: red in `stock_source_law` (`engrave_and_trace_off_the_stock_...`, `the_typed_kinds_and_face_...`) and in `neighbour_law::a_cut_on_b_into_its_neighbour_...`. Without the skip, the by-name gouge refusal is displaced.
4. `marks` forced false (the mark law not used for a stock-source mark): red in `stock_source_law::a_legal_stock_source_cut_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks`. The re-judge would refuse a legal mark.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1607-stock-source-law` on 329db7d8: green (app suites 1227 s, ui suites 152 s, 0 failed). Clippy on `camcraft-app` (`--lib --tests -D warnings`) is clean.

## Not exercised
- 3+2 (tilted) ops: the cached world path is judged in the frame's local coordinates, as chords at the arc-fit tolerance. No suite has a clean tilted 2D op beside another part, so this arm is not covered by a test.
- The fail-closed arm for "the job cannot be collected again" is unreachable by any fixture: every input `collect_job` can fail on is a stamp input, so such an op reads Stale first.
- Un-marking raw-stock-only after generation goes through the same live set (`stock_source::judged`). It has no dedicated pin here.

Changelog: A part moved into, added to, or un-tagged inside an operation's cut after generation no longer posts on a turned stock: the post judges the parts beside each op's source again and refuses by name (#1628)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1628

title: fix(2d): judge a stock-source cross drill against the parts in its stock
body:
stacked on #1634 - review only after 881f7726; merge #1615, #1622, #1634 first. (fork synced at v0.18.0)

## What was found (reproduced before any fix)

#1635 asked whether a stock-source cross drill that enters a part posts unjudged. It does not. `cross_part::part_clear` read the source's mesh, and off the stock that mesh is the stock itself. So EVERY stock-source cross drill was refused at generation, the illegal ones and the legal ones alike, with "cross hole ... rapids into the finished part". The stock was read as the solid to keep. Nothing reached the post, so this is not a P1. It is a false refusal of legal programs, which is P3 by the AGENTS.md table (left at P1 for the maintainer to lower).

Readings: #117 punched bar r10 with one r2 hole plunging -X from (10, 0, 0), 6 mm deep. Stocks: an r20 bar and a 40 x 40 box, each aligned and turned a quarter about Z. Mill-turn and lathe benches. Stock-source op S1.

| case | before (all four stocks) | now |
|---|---|---|
| hole where the bar models none | refused: "rapids into the finished part" (meaning the stock) | refused: "cuts into the finished part: the drill meets steel at the mouth - the model has no hole there" |
| into the bar's modelled hole | refused, same words | generates the part source's chain, move for move; posts |
| stock-only material (r3 core) | refused, same words | generates; posts |
| lathe, box stock, legal hole | refused: "cannot be read as turned" (that is the box) | generates |

## What changed

- `cross_spindle::cross_drill` takes `Solids { source, stock, kept }`.
  - On a part source: unchanged (the part, the setup's stock, the part).
  - On a stock source: the setup's parts are the solid it measures and keeps, and the source stock is the raw material its mouths stand off. This is exactly the chain a part-source cross drill drills in that stock.
- `keep_law::is_cross_drill` joins `is_stock_kept_kind`, so `parts_in_stock` returns the setup's parts for it. Fixtures and a stock-only model are left out.
- The 2D tail's vertical solid law against those parts skips a cross drill (`parts_crossed`). The radial law has already judged the chain, and the solid law with no wall excuse would convict a drill sized to a faceted cross hole.
- On a plain lathe, a stock-source cross drill reads the parts as the turned work, not the box stock.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1635-stock-cross-drill.md`.

## How tested

Pins in `crates/app/tests/stock_source_cross_drill.rs` (new):
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_into_the_part_is_refused_by_name_on_both_stocks`
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_into_the_parts_own_hole_or_stock_only_material_posts` (also asserts the chain equals the part source's)
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_at_the_modelled_holes_size_is_excused_its_faceted_wall`
- `a_stock_source_cross_drill_with_no_part_in_the_setup_keeps_nothing`
- `a_lathe_reads_the_turned_part_in_a_box_stock_not_the_box`
- `over_mcp_a_stock_source_cross_drill_answers_for_the_part_the_same` (built-in Mill-turn, MCP's default Stock source)

Six mutations, each checked red and then reverted. The table is in the decision file.

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on da340c0f: sim 102 s, motion 6 s, app 1262 s, ui 59 s, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The 3+2 frame arm's `parts_crossed` guard. A cross drill is lathe or mill-turn work and does not reach that arm.
- A posted program on a plain lathe. The bench mounts no turning post.
- MCP on a turned stock. MCP's `set_stock` takes no rotation.

## Follow-up

A part-source cross drill still answers only to its own source, not to #1621's neighbouring parts.

Changelog: A cross drill taken off the stock is judged against the parts the stock holds, not against the stock: drilling a part's own cross hole off the raw bar now generates and posts, and a hole into a part where it models none is refused by name (#1635).
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1635

title: feat(ui): the CamCraft UI workbench rework
body:
### Summary

CamCraft's UI gets its workbench rework, built on upstream v0.19.0. It gives the shell a light workbench theme (`horizon-day`), puts a tab row above the ribbon cells to switch machine modes in one click, gives the operation page's section tabs their own glyphs, tightens the browser's chrome and row order, and adds camera tools to the viewport's floating control ribbon.

Five commits, one topic each:

- `feat(ui): a light workbench theme and workspace tabs`
- `feat(ui): the operation page's section tabs wear their own glyphs`
- `feat(ui): a compact browser header and ordered rows`
- `feat(ui): camera tools in the viewport's control ribbon`
- `refactor(ui): drop the Machine ribbon cell - the workspace tabs own the switch`

### What to look at

- The ribbon gains a workspace tab row above the cells: one tab per machine mode in `machine_modes::MACHINE_MODES`, switching through the same undoable `LoadBuiltinMachine` the Machine door queued. The stocked door and the tabs were two doors onto one switch; the tabs won, and the SETUP group sheds the redundant "Machine" cell at the end. The Machine door's code path remains present but unreachable from the UI, held for a follow-up removal pass.
- `assets/themes/horizon-day.json` is a light "Horizon Day" palette (base light) that users can pick from the Theme door; nothing switches the default theme - dark stays the default.
- The section tabs in the operation pages wear purpose-drawn `sec-*` glyphs (six SVG masters, rendered at the ribbon's token size; our own artwork); the ribbon cell ink gains a tinted-palette hook with a steel-blue tint for command glyphs.
- The viewport's floating control ribbon gains four buttons: a Perspective/Orthographic toggle (the View door's radios' true twin), and a latched Orbit/Pan/Zoom nav tool that owns the drag whatever the mouse button - a latched tool's click is no click at all.
- The browser heads with one chrome row (a View door, Expand all / Collapse all) and the setup's furniture leads the rows: Setups, WCS, Stock, Operations, Tool list, Fixtures, Machine, Post.

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 772 passed. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` - green (ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --lib --tests` - no warnings.

Known flake: the palette/assertion law tests are parallel-order dependent - a full parallel run can see a handful of them fail while `--test-threads=1` is all green; the failure set moves between runs, and serial runs pass. Nothing in this PR changes their behaviour; re-run to confirm.

title: fix(import): mesh rational B-spline thread strips closed and at full fidelity
body:
## What changed

The rational `B_SPLINE_SURFACE` faces of #1602's parts are thread flanks and roots. Each is one strip, degree 1 across and degree 2 along, in 36-degree arcs, about fourteen turns long. truck meshed each one into ~2 M facets with a 0.5-3 mm hole. Three causes, all fixed in the importer's wrapper around a face (`step_guard::Metered`), with truck itself unchanged:

1. **Facet runaway: the division split both directions.** truck's `parameter_division` flags BOTH intervals of a cell that fails its bilinear test. A strip curved only along v therefore gets 2^sweeps intervals across u. The new `step_division` tests each cell's iso-v chord (splits u) and iso-u chord (splits v) separately, and it falls back to truck's bilinear test (which splits both) only for a twist. Every cell of the result still passes truck's acceptance test. A division that is still splitting after 64 sweeps (a jump) spends the face's evaluation budget, so it is refused by name exactly as before (#1536). It never comes back as a grid with a wall in it.
2. **Slivers: the parameter plane was 350x too short across.** truck triangulates a trimmed face by constrained Delaunay in (u, v). With nothing to constrain the plane next to the boundary, the empty-circle rule joined boundary points to the far ends of the strip. The new `step_stretch` stretches the faster parameter of a B-spline/NURBS face by its mean-speed ratio, so the mesher's plane has about the same proportions as the face. A face within 4:1 is untouched.
3. **The hole: boundary points found on the wrong turn.** truck's no-hint presearch (a 51 x 51 grid) samples a 14-turn strip about three times a turn, and Newton then settles one pitch off, outside the knot domain. On a root band the extrapolated rulings meet other turns exactly, at u = 7 on [0, 1]. The new `step_nearest` re-searches any answer that is off the surface or outside the domain. It starts Newton from the nearest samples of a grid that has up to 4 samples in every knot span (<= 4,096 evaluations), and takes the nearest answer inside the domain. Poles are settled by `step_pole` first (#1548), as before.

Decision entry: `docs/decisions/1602-thread-strip-mesh.md`.

## Readings (release; the user's files stay local)

| File | upstream main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 10208.STEP | 6,095,454 facets, chord 0.0157 mm (reduced), 31-72 s | **13,662 facets, chord 0.005 mm, 1.9 s** |
| 32050.STEP | 4,970,604 facets, 62-130 s | **8,128 facets, chord 0.005 mm, 1.8 s** |
| sc_logo.step | 36,728 facets, 0.19 s | 34,496 facets, 0.19 s, 0 open edges |
| synthetic 14-turn flank (a scratch generator) | 7,540,126 facets, 248 s, 3.3 GB | 3,072 facets, 0.8 s |
| the test's 4-turn trimmed flank | 471,695 facets, 7.3 s | 861 facets, 0.08 s |
| testdata/models/*.step | | facet counts unchanged |

**Closed-shell check:** I trial-merged PR #1576's head (e7d78efe) locally, without pushing it. Both parts import closed and pass its check. Before this change that check refused them: 10208 at face #1073 (up to 3.0 mm) and 32050 at faces #3350 and #5466. The gaps #1576's check still reported on these files are this issue's faces, and they are gone now.

## Pinning tests

title: fix(post): Fanuc-family mill posts state the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

The second half of #1616 (PR #1632 did grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera; #1618 set the rule and wording on Tormach). `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `sinumerik.cps` and `heidenhain.cps` no longer write the first move after `G43 H..` (or the TNC tool call) as one combined rapid from wherever the tool change left the tip. At the program's start and after every tool change, the first motion is preceded by:

1. a Z-only rapid to the section's `ClearancePlane`, else its `RetractPlane`, never below the move's own Z;
2. X/Y alone at that height (left out when the first rapid already is at that height - it is then the traverse itself);
3. for a feed, arc or probing move, a rapid down to the stream's start Z when that is lower;

then the move as the stream states it. A canned cycle read as the first motion is positioned over its hole at the stated height first. A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, and **the refused move is not written** - nor any later motion of that section while X/Y stay unknown (the rest of the section is refused cleanly; review of this PR), so no combined `G00 X.. Y.. Z..` from an unknown height reaches the program text. The wording is #1618/#1632's: `first X/Y traverse with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) - the post will not rapid X/Y at an unknown height` (prefixed `operation <name>: ` where the post knows it).

Each dialect writes its own rapid: `G00 Z..` (Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan), `G0 Z..` (Haas, 840D). The Heidenhain post is the TNC's ISO dialect, so its form is `G00 G40 G90 Z+..*` - the manual's own positioning block (the section's first motion block carries G40 G90), not `L Z.. FMAX`.

The issue's example, `synth_fanuc.nc`: `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3` after `G43 H02` is now `G00 Z5` / `G00 X20 Y10` / `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3`.

### Frame decision: G43.4 / TCP and rotary paths - correct in the frame, not refused

Recorded in `docs/decisions/1633-fanuc-first-traverse-clearance.md`.
- **Fanuc and Doosan, tilted first record (G43.4):** the rapids are written after the record's own `tilt()`, i.e. after `G43.4 H..` is armed. Z is then the tip's Z in the work offset - the frame the stream states its planes and words in. No rotary word rides the inserted blocks; the rotaries turn only on the record itself, at its target, as before.
- **Doosan indexing path (4th axis, no TCP):** the rapids are in G43 (the frame of the record's own words) with the table still clamped; the index (M11, the move, M10) is the record's.
- **Haas, Mazak, 840D, TNC:** they refuse tilted records (`tiltOk`), so the rapids are always upright.
- Dropped: refusing a tilted first record whose pose is unknown (every rapid of a real rotary program states its pose, so every 5-axis program would be refused at its start); writing the Z before the G43.4 arm (G43 is machine-Z length comp, so a tilted tip would not be at the stated height); inserting the Z line alone (the diagonal from clearance to a first target below the stock top would still cross the part).

## How tested

Pinning suite (new): `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family.rs`, #1632's five-test shape over all six posts plus four:
- `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first`
- `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated`
- `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` (also asserts no X/Y motion - neither the bare traverse nor the combined rapid - is written after the refusal, for every post)
- `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height`
- `a_feed_first_move_rapids_down_from_the_stated_clearance`
- `a_cycle_first_is_positioned_over_its_hole_at_the_stated_clearance`
- `the_tnc_states_the_height_in_its_positioning_block_form`
- `under_g43_4_the_height_is_stated_after_the_arm_and_before_any_turn` (fanuc, doosan-dnm on the tilthead)
- `on_the_doosan_index_path_the_height_is_stated_with_the_table_clamped`

Also re-pinned: `fanuc_post::rtcp_output_arms_once_and_walks_the_angles` (the `G00 Z5` sits right after `G43.4 H01`), `doosan_dnm_post::doosan_dnm_index_names_only_a_stated_rotary` (`G00 Z10` before `M11`), `heidenhain_cycles::g200_uses_surface_relative_q_values_and_keeps_the_explicit_hop` (`G00 G40 G90 Z-40`, then `G00 X+10 Y+20`).

### Mutations (each restored after)

Per post, run against `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family`:

| post | drop the Z line | replace the refusal |
|---|---|---|
| fanuc | 6 red (incl. the G43.4 frame test) | `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` red |
| haas | 5 red | refusal test red |
| mazak | 5 red | refusal test red |
| doosan-dnm | 7 red (incl. G43.4 frame and index-path tests) | refusal test red |
| sinumerik | 5 red | refusal test red |
| heidenhain | 6 red (incl. the TNC block-form test) | refusal test red |

Putting the write back after the refusal (`if (!xyFirst(..)) return;` -> `xyFirst(..);`): `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` red for each of the six posts.

### Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final tree: post suites ok, app suites ok (all app suites ran: shared test code changed), 14.5 min, 0 failed.

Hand-written streams that stated no plane now state one, as `post::dump` does for every real section (comp, comp_plane, axis_direction_cli, work_offset_index, heidenhain_cycles, heidenhain_block_form, heidenhain_arc_centre, doosan_dnm_post, fanuc_post, vendor_mch_cli, arc_planes, inverted_support; app: doosan_dnm_a_state, fourth_axis_pose, rotary_feed_cap, program_units, sinumerik_safe_retract, sinumerik_work_offsets). `regression_models` line counts +1 each (the stated height). The test readers `macro_b` (inverted_probe) and `inverted_support::controller_events` (inverted_equivalence) now read a Z-only move before X/Y are known as the stated height, not a move from an unknown position / a CAM motion. `crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/inverted_probe.cnc` regenerated (one added `PARAM ClearancePlane`).

title: fix(2d): judge a stock-source Chamfer, Drill, Bore or Thread against the parts in the stock
body:
**Stacked on #1622 - review only the commits after c74d888d (ae1651db, 881f7726); merge #1615 then #1622 first.** Fork synced at v0.19.0; branch made from #1622's head c74d888d.

A stock-source 2D Chamfer, Drill, Bore or Thread stayed at `DepthLaw::None` (#1607 left them out of `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind`), so a cut into a part held in the stock had 0 op findings: aligned, the program sim held the post; turned, **it posted**.

## What changed
- `keep_law::is_hole_kind` (new): Drill without cross holes, Bore, Thread. `is_stock_kept_kind` now holds these and `Chamfer2D`, so `parts_in_stock` collects the setup's parts for them (fixtures and a stock-only model left out, as #1607).
- `run_job`, both frame arms:
  - **Hole kinds:** the **containment law** against the parts (`contain_into` with `DepthLaw::Contain`). This is the law a part-source hole already answers to. It excuses only the round wall of each declared hole, measured about that hole's axis to the facets' sagitta (#1205), plus a thread mill's declared bore (#1071). A hole where the part models none, one wider than the part's hole, or one deeper than its floor is a blocking `Gouge`.
  - **2D Chamfer:** the **solid law** (`Keep`, nothing excused).
- **Tap core re-read (#266):** the closure that re-judges a Tap cycle's gouges at its core now also re-reads the stock-source parts and #1621's neighbours. Before, any gouge the core run did not raise was dropped. That run read only the source's own law, so those parts' gouges were acquitted without being checked. This is a #1622 gap fixed here because it shares the same lines. A part-source tap through a neighbouring lid that models no hole had 0 gouges before and is convicted now.

### Why the solid law for the Chamfer, not a mark-style budget
On a part source the chamfer breaks the part's own edge, which is legal by construction (#303 credits the declared break). Off the stock, the edge it follows is the **stock's** edge. A stock edge clear of every part meets no part facet, so the solid law finds nothing. A stock edge on or inside a part cuts a break into the part that no part edge declared. A mark-style budget (the part lowered by the chamfer depth) would allow a V-groove of that depth anywhere a stock edge crosses a part's face, which is the gouge this issue is about. The chamfer depth is also derived, not a number the user stated as permission. Cost: a chamfer off a stock **flush** with the part (box stock = the part's footprint) is now refused on the op, although the sim credits the break and it posted before. The workaround is to chamfer with the part as the source, which gives the same path and is legal there.

## Readings
Probe on c74d888d and on this branch. 30 x 30 x 20 plate with one modelled round hole; square box stock flush with its top, aligned or turned a quarter about Z.

| stock-source case | before: S1 gouges · aligned / turned | now: S1 gouges · aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|
| Drill Ø6 at (0, 9), no hole there / 3 mm under the r 3 hole's floor | 0 · refused by sim / **posts** | 1 · refused / refused by S1's moves |
| M6 Tap at (0, 9) / 3 mm past the Ø5 hole's floor | 0 · refused by sim / **posts** | 2 · refused / refused |
| Bore r 5 at (0, 9) / Bore r 6 in the r 5 hole | 0 · refused by sim / **posts** | 12 / 10 · refused / refused |
| Thread at (0, 9.5) / 4 mm under the hole's floor | 0 · refused by sim | 31 · refused (turned: never generates, #992) |
| Chamfer 1 mm, stock flush with the part | 0 · **posts / posts** | 5 · refused / refused |
| Part-source tap through a lid part (#1621 neighbour) | 0 | 2 |
| Drill / tap / bore / thread at the part's hole to size; the same at (25, 0) in stock-only material; chamfer on a 70 x 70 stock | 0 · posts | 0 · posts / posts (thread: aligned only) |

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs` (6; fixtures in `stock_source_holes_support/`):
- `a_hole_kind_off_the_stock_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`: drill, tap, bore and thread, each both nowhere and too deep or too wide, on both stocks. The turned-stock thread is refused by name at generation.
- `a_hole_kind_in_the_parts_own_hole_or_in_stock_only_material_posts`: the part's hole is modelled as a 32-gon, so a tool at size passes only through the wall excuse.
- `a_chamfer_off_a_stock_flush_with_the_part_gouges_and_one_clear_of_it_posts`
- `a_tap_through_a_neighbouring_part_is_not_acquitted_at_its_core`
- `a_stock_source_hole_or_chamfer_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `over_mcp_a_stock_source_hole_or_chamfer_answers_for_the_part_the_same`: MCP `add_operation` (default source: the stock), `generate`, `verify`. Drill into the part, in its hole and in stock-only material; chamfer flush and clear.

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | red |
|---|---|
| M1 the four kinds out of `is_stock_kept_kind` | into-part, chamfer, MCP |
| M2 hole kinds judged by the plain solid law | into-part, legal, MCP |
| M3 Chamfer out only | chamfer, MCP |
| M4 stock-source parts out of the tap core re-read | into-part (tap) |
| M5 neighbours out of the tap core re-read | tap-through-lid |
| M6 no thread bore granted against the parts | legal (thread) |
| M7 `Keep` instead of `Contain` (no wall excuse) | legal, MCP |

No existing test changed; no golden or snapshot changes.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 881f7726 (sim 101 s, motion 5 s, app 1179 s, ui 48 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised
- The 3+2 frame arm with a stock-source hole or chamfer (same shape as #1607's arm).
- MCP on a turned stock (`set_stock` takes no rotation).
- A Thread off a turned stock never generates (#992's way-in law cannot read the program ahead there; this happens on a part source too). Pinned as it stands, not changed.
- The cross drill (a Drill with cross holes) on a stock source: its chain answers to `cross_part` against the source's mesh, not the setup's parts. Follow-up #1635 (P1).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1631-stock-holes-chamfer.md`.

MCP: no new command or tool; `add_operation` / `generate` / `verify` reach the law (pinned).

Changelog: A 2D Drill, Bore or Thread whose source is the stock is judged against the parts standing in that stock - it may enter a part only through the hole the part models there, to its size and depth - and a stock-source 2D Chamfer by the solid law, so a cut into a part is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused even where the program sim cannot judge; a tap's core re-read no longer acquits a gouge in a neighbouring or stock-held part (#1631).

title: fix(post): grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera state the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

The #1614 hazard in three more mill posts. After a tool change, and at the start of the program, `grblhal.cps`, `tinyg.cps` and `carvera.cps` used to write a bare `G0 X.. Y..` at whatever height the change left the tool tip. With a long tool on a high work offset, the tip can be below the part top at that height. grblHAL and TinyG now state that height, as `tormach.cps` does in #1618. The Carvera states it at a program start, but not before its first X/Y traverse after `M6` (see below):

- The traverse is at the section's `ClearancePlane`, or its `RetractPlane` when no clearance plane is stated. It is never below the move's own Z.
- **grblHAL and TinyG** write the Z-only `G0 Z` first, then the bare X/Y, then the descent.
- **Carvera (M3's option (c))** writes it in one of two orders:
  - Right after `M6 T..`: X/Y first, at the changer's exit height (main's order), then `G0 Z<clearance>`, then the descent. Nothing we have read says where the firmware parks X/Y after a tool change. A Z-only rapid down to a thin stock's clearance at that X/Y could meet the tools stored in the rack.
  - **The #1614 hazard stays for the Carvera after `M6`.** The bare X/Y traverse after `M6` is still made at the changer's exit height, and nothing we have read confirms that height. A long tool can leave the tip below the part top there, and the traverse then crosses the part. The hazard stays open until a public source confirms the firmware's `M6` exit position (option b). The comment in `carvera.cps` and the decision file say so.
  - At a program start with no tool change: Z first, like the other two posts.
- A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, with #1618's wording: "first X/Y traverse with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) - the post will not rapid X/Y at an unknown height". The operation name is added in front when the post knows it.
- When a feed is the first move, the existing rapid down to its start height is skipped if the traverse already went to that height. Before this change TinyG wrote that rapid every time.
- The planes are read per section and reset at the end of each section, as in #1618.
- The comments in all three posts that described X/Y first at the changer or safe height now match the code.

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` is not touched. #1618 and the #1626 branch own it.

`crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs` gets the same hunk as #1618, line for line (checked by diff), so the two PRs merge cleanly. This is how the legacy goldens state their clearance from their `START` height.

**This PR does not close #1616 (`Refs #1616`).** Two parts of its "Done means" stay open: the Fanuc-family half (fanuc, haas, mazak, doosan-dnm, sinumerik, heidenhain), which is #1633, and the Carvera after `M6`. The Fanuc-family posts have no `xyUnknown` traverse; they write the combined first rapid after `G43`, and they carry G43.4 and rotary paths. I did not add the rule to `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: #1618 adds a bullet at the same spot, so editing it here would conflict. #1633 widens the bullet's list of posts. Option (c), the options considered and these choices are recorded in `docs/decisions/1616-first-traverse-clearance.md`.

## Moved goldens: 57 files, one added `G0 Z` line each (two in the two-tool programs)

I checked every moved golden by diff against `main`, not by a blanket regenerate. Each one gains only the clearance `G0 Z` line, and no line was removed or changed. A script confirmed where the added line sits:
- grblHAL and TinyG: right before the bare `G0 X.. Y..` traverse.
- Carvera: right after it, because each of these programs starts with `M6 T..`.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/{grblhal,carvera,tinyg}/` (12 legacy goldens each): `+G0 Z5`, or `+G0 Z6` for `drill_peck`. That is the golden's START or clearance height.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_{grblhal,carvera,tinyg}.nc`: `+G0 Z5`. The synth stream's ClearancePlane is 10 and OriginZ is 5.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/grblhal/altmill_4x4_two_tool{,_inch}.nc`: `+G0 Z15` (or `Z0.5906`) after each of the two tool changes.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/carvera/two_tool_pocket.nc`: `+G0 Z5` after `G0 X5 Y5` and again after `G0 X20 Y25`, after each `M6`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/{grblhal,carvera,tinyg}/{arcs,drill_retract,extreme_coords,full_circle,full_circle_raw}.nc`: `+G0 Z50`, or `+G0 Z10` for `drill_retract`.
- `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/grblhal.nc`: `+G0 Z10` before the first `G0 X10 Y10`, which follows `G53 G0 Z0` / `T3 M6`.

In this round, the 19 Carvera goldens moved again: the `G0 Z` line now comes after the X/Y line that follows `M6`. On grblHAL and TinyG without `safe_retract`, the lift before the change already goes to the same work-offset height, so the added line repeats it. I kept it on purpose: the tool change itself (a manual change, a tool setter, a jog at TinyG's M0) can move Z.

## Tests

- Pinning suite `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance.rs`, run over all three posts on shipped machines (AltMill 2x4, TinyG 3-axis, Makera Carvera). Each post's traverse order is pinned: Z then X/Y, except Carvera after `M6`, which is X/Y then Z.
  - `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z`
  - `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated`
  - `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height`
  - `a_feed_first_move_rapids_down_from_the_stated_clearance`
  - `at_the_program_start_with_no_tool_change_the_clearance_z_comes_first` (new; all three posts, Carvera included)
- Existing tests whose streams stated no plane now state one, as `post::dump` does: `grblhal_post.rs`, `tinyg_post.rs`, `altmill_machines.rs`, `carvera_post.rs`, `post_spindle_rule_all.rs`. Two `G0 Z15` counts went up by the two stated traverses (grblhal 3 to 5, tinyg 5 to 7). The grblhal test now also checks that `G0 Z15` comes right before the `G0 X20 Y5` traverse.

**Mutation checks.** I mutated each post separately and ran the pinning suite. Every mutation turned it red:

| Mutation | Applied to | Tests that went red |
|---|---|---|
| M1: drop the `G0 Z<tz>` line | each post | 5 of 6 (all except the refusal test) |
| M2: replace the refusal with Z0 (`if (c === null) c = 0;`) | each post | `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` |
| M3: drop the same-height check | each post | `a_feed_first_move_rapids_down_from_the_stated_clearance` |
| M4: swap the order back to Z-first after `M6` (`if (changedAt)` changed to `if (false)`) | Carvera | 4 tests (tool change, retract plane, never below, feed first) |
| M5: X/Y first at program start too (`if (true)`) | Carvera | `at_the_program_start_with_no_tool_change_the_clearance_z_comes_first` |

After restoring the files, all 6 tests pass.

**Gate.** On a1833e52, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: post suites 22 s, app suites 1000 s, 0 failed. The change touches shared test input, so the quick tier ran nearly every app suite. The `import_step_guard` flake did not show. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No PathPilot Hub, grblHAL, TinyG or Carvera hardware or sender run. The output was read from the goldens only.
- The Carvera firmware's `M6` exit position (X, Y and Z) was not read from any documentation. That is why it gets option (c), and why the #1614 hazard stays open for the Carvera after `M6`.
- The Fanuc family is not changed; that is #1633.

Branched from upstream `main` at c00ba18a (fork worktree).

Changelog: grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera posts state the section's clearance Z (ClearancePlane, else RetractPlane) before the first descent after a tool change (Carvera: after its X/Y traverse at the changer's exit height, which stays unverified), and refuse a stream that states neither by name (#1616)

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(project): a typed hole floor no longer reads Stale after save and reopen
body:
## What changed

A Bore op (or Drill, or Thread) whose hole list was edited to a value off the 1 um lattice - the issue's floor typed as `0.190 in - 0.040 in` = `3.8099999999999996` mm - read **Stale** after save and reopen. The file stores the hole as `3.81` (`HoleDto::from_hole` snaps to the lattice), but the stamp taken at generate hashed the unsnapped bits.

- New `crates/app/src/operation/hole_digest.rs`: one hole (and one radial hole) digested with every float snapped by `cl::lattice`, the same snap `HoleDto` / `CrossHoleDto` apply when the file writes the list. The radial `dir` stays verbatim, as the file keeps it. Byte order per hole is unchanged.
- `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`: the Drill (holes + cross), Bore and Thread arms of `stamp_with` call it instead of hashing raw bits (the file shrinks by 28 lines).
- On-lattice holes (everything `detect_holes` emits) hash bit-for-bit as before, so no stamp that matched before changes. A change of half a micron or more still moves the stamp (unit-pinned). No project-file version bump, no posted-output change, no golden or snapshot change.
- Same remedy as #1351 / PR #1352 (`path_sig` hashes moves on the lattice). Snapping at the edit command, the brief's first preference, was dropped: the snap would have to be repeated at every door a hole list comes through (create, edit, paste, GUI table, scripts, old files) and would move the generator's input - the reason #1352 dropped snapping in `Toolpath::new`. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1560-hole-digest-lattice.md`.

## Pins (mutation-checked: `put` hashing raw bits -> all three red; restored -> green)

- `bore_entry::an_edited_hole_floor_off_the_lattice_stays_ok_through_save_and_load` - through the commands: `CreateOperation` Bore, `EditOperationParams` with the off-lattice floor, `GenerateOperation`, `project::save`, `project::load` into a fresh world -> `OpStatus::Ok` (mutant: `Stale`).
- `bore_core::an_edited_hole_floor_off_the_lattice_reopens_ok_and_posts_the_same` - the issue's MCP flow: `detect_holes`, `edit_operation` with `floor_z` 3.8099999999999996 / blind, `generate`, `post` (Fanuc), `save_project`, `open_project` in a new server -> `get_job` status `ok` (mutant: `stale`), and the posted program after reopen is byte-identical to the one before the save.
- `operation::hole_digest::tests::a_typed_floor_stamps_like_the_one_the_file_reloads` - typed and reloaded floors digest alike; 3.81 vs 3.811 still differ.

## Sweep (other DTOs that call `lattice(...)` at save)

- Params: only `HoleDto` and `CrossHoleDto` snap at save - both covered here (Drill holes + radial holes, Bore, Thread). Every other params float is written verbatim (serde's shortest form round-trips the bits, #169).
- Cached-output DTOs (`MoveDto`, `CompSpanDto`, the drill-cycle DTO, `ThreadCycleDto`, the edge-break DTO) store a generated cache, not stamp inputs. The moves feed `path_sig`, already lattice since #1352; nothing else digests the spans, cycles or breaks (grepped every `Hasher` user in `crates/app/src`). No follow-up issue needed.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, sccache): green - wall 10.1 min, 2 steps, 0 failed (it ran every app/ui suite the gate maps name for `app::operation`).
- Named suites, again on their own: app lib (238), project_roundtrip (73), bore_core (5), bore_entry (4), face_holes, operations, mcp, commands_undo, posting, float_roundtrip - 514 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Fork synced at upstream/main c00ba18a.

## Not exercised

- A file already saved before this fix, with a stamp taken from an off-lattice hole, still reads Stale once on reopen; one regenerate stores the new stamp (no re-stamp on load, by design).
- The GUI hole table (it goes through the same `EditOperationParams` and the same stamp).
- Batch and release tiers; Windows.

title: fix(2d): judge a stock-source cut against the parts in the stock, whatever its kind
body:
**Stacked on #1615 - review only the commits after 4f05e9c0 (#1615's head, merged in at 3b532fac); merge #1615 first.** Fork synced at v0.19.0; branch made from #1615's head 976cda6c (upstream main f2b42e3d plus #1615), then #1615's review fix 4f05e9c0 merged in. Also fixes #1621 (P1) on the same branch: it touches the same `keep_parts` lines in `run_job`.

A 2D operation whose source is the **stock** (or a pick off it) carried no part law: `part_solid` is false, so `depth_law_of` returned `DepthLaw::None` before the kind's arm. A cut into the part held in that stock had 0 op findings: the program sim held it on an aligned stock, and on a turned stock (the sim refuses to judge) it posted.

## What changed
- `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind` (new): every 2D kind that carries a part law on a part source - the pocket family (as #1603), Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, Contour, Face, Engrave, Trace. `keep_law::parts_in_stock` now collects the setup's parts (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`: every part, fixtures and a stock-only model left out) for all of them.
- `run_job` (`generate.rs`, both the plain and the 3+2 frame branch): on those parts, Engrave and Trace take the **mark law** (`mark_law::mark_into`, budget `min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`), every other kind the **solid law** (`contain_into`, nothing excused).
- `mark_law::budget_of`: a stock-source Engrave or Trace declares its mark too, so the program sim credits exactly what the op's law allows (before, the sim judged a stock-source mark against the sharp model: a 0.3 mm mark along the part's outline was refused on an aligned stock).
- A setup with no part judges nothing, as before. Paths are unchanged; only the verdict.

## Readings
#1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, EM-0600-4FL) in a 40 x 40 x 8 box stock over it, aligned and turned 90 deg about Z:

| stock-source case | before: op gouges, aligned / turned | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engrave / Trace Top 8, Bottom 1 (the part's outside wall), Stock or stock top picked | 0, refused by sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular in the pocket 3 mm under its floor | 0, refused by sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Face to Z5 (3 mm into the part's top) | 0, refused by sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Engrave / Trace 0.3 mm along the part's outline | 0, **refused by sim** / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| Contour round the stock to Z1; Slot in the pocket to its floor; Face of a 10 mm stock to Z8 | 0, posts / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| Two parts in one stock, Slot / Trochoidal slot into either part | 0 | yes | refused / refused |

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/stock_source_law.rs` (6; generate, then post; both stocks):
- `engrave_and_trace_off_the_stock_down_the_part_wall_gouge_and_never_post` (Stock and a pick of the stock's top; the mark note named)
- `the_typed_kinds_and_face_off_the_stock_into_the_part_gouge_and_never_post` (Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, Face)
- `a_legal_stock_source_cut_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks` (Engrave, Trace, Contour, Slot, Face)
- `a_stock_source_cut_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `a_stock_source_cut_answers_for_every_part_in_the_stock` (two parts; a cut into either is convicted)
- `over_mcp_a_stock_source_cut_answers_for_the_part_the_same` (MCP `add_operation` source `stock`, `generate`, `verify`: Engrave, Trace deep and legal; Face into the part)

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | red |
|---|---|
| M1 `parts_in_stock` back to the pocket family only | 11 (the 4 new refusal pins incl. MCP and two-part, and the 7 restated tests) |
| M2 Engrave / Trace judged by the solid law, not the mark law | 4 (legal marks, deep marks, MCP, engrave_law stock pin) |
| M3 sim credit back off for a Stock source | 3 (legal marks post, MCP, sim credit) |
| M4 the mark law not run against the parts | 3 (deep marks, MCP, engrave_law stock pin) |
| M5 only the first part read (`take(1)`) | 1 (two-part) |
| M5b only the last part read | 1 (two-part) |

## Merged with #1615's review fix (4f05e9c0)
#1615 changed `mark_into` to return `Marked` (deep / through / stack) and the note to `mark_law::notes(...)`, and added the material floor (`MARK_FLOOR`, `verify::seat_skin`) and the unlowered shank/holder stack check. Both `run_job` call sites conflicted with this branch's stock-source mark law. Resolution: the mark law picks its mesh as before (the source part on `DepthLaw::Mark`, the setup's parts on a stock-source Engrave / Trace) and passes it to the one `mark_into`, so the floor and the stack check apply to the stock source too; the notes come from `mark_law::notes` in both frame arms. `budget_of` keeps this branch's reading (no `names_part`), `keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind` / `keep_parts` unchanged.
- Pin: `mark_floor.rs::a_stock_source_cut_through_the_plate_meets_the_same_floor` - a Stock-source Engrave / Trace 2.9 mm and 1.9 mm through the 2 mm plate refused by name ("cuts through the part") on both stocks; 0.3 mm posts.

## #1621: a part-source cut answers for the setup's other parts
A part-source op's law read only its source's mesh, so a cut on part B entering part A beside it had no op finding. Measured before (B the #1585 pocket block on x [0,40], A a box on x [-40,-0.7], 80 x 80 x 8 stock): a 0.3 mm Trace / Engrave round B (flank 2.3 mm into A) **posted on both stocks** (the sim credits A the mark budget too); a Contour outside B to Z1 was refused by the sim aligned and **posted turned**.
- `keep_law::neighbour_parts` (new): for a part-source op that carries a part law (`depth_law_of(params, src, true) != None` - Contour, Face, Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, pocket family, Drill without cross, Bore, Thread, Engrave, Trace), the setup's parts (`parts_facets_in`'s set: fixtures and a stock-only model left out) less the entities its source names. Carried on `GenJob::neighbour_parts`.
- `run_job`, both frame arms: those parts take the plain solid law (`contain_into` with `Keep`: nothing excused, no mark budget). The source keeps its own law (Mark budget on the part being marked; Section / Keep / Contain as before).
- Behaviour to know: a whole-model 2D pocket on B in a stock that also holds A clears through A and is now convicted on the op (a real gouge of A).

Pins, `crates/app/tests/neighbour_law.rs` (5; generate, then post; aligned and quarter-turned stock):
- `a_cut_on_b_into_its_neighbour_gouges_on_the_op_and_never_posts` (Trace, Engrave, Contour; gouge on a move that reaches A; turned: refused by the op's moves)
- `a_mark_on_b_within_its_budget_clear_of_a_posts_on_both_stocks` (whole B and B's top picked)
- `a_mark_on_b_deeper_than_its_budget_is_still_judged_by_its_own_law`
- `a_pocket_on_bs_own_floor_is_unchanged_beside_a_neighbour` (same path and findings as with A far away; posts)
- `over_mcp_a_cut_on_b_answers_for_its_neighbour_the_same` (MCP `import_model` x2, `add_operation` source `part`, `generate`, `verify`)
- `area_controls.rs::a_boundary_offset_on_a_tilted_pocket_is_the_flat_offset_pocket_rotated` now also asserts the tower beside the tilted (3+2) pocket is convicted on the op (the neighbour law's frame arm)

## Mutations (each alone, then reverted)
| job | mutation | red |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `seat_skin` emptied (no floor) | `a_stock_source_cut_through_the_plate_meets_the_same_floor` |
| 2 | M1 `neighbour_parts` always empty | into-neighbour pin, MCP pin (2) |

| 2 | M3 neighbours judged by the mark law with B's budget | into-neighbour pin, MCP pin (2) |

| 2 | M5 the source's own law stood down when a neighbour exists | deep-mark pin (1) |
| 2 | M7 the neighbour law dropped from the 3+2 frame arm | `area_controls` tilted-pocket test (1) |

The pocket pin is a no-false-positive guard (same path and findings with and without A); none of M1-M5 turns it red, and no plausible mutation found makes it the only one red - recorded honestly.

## Existing tests that changed
Each asserted "a stock source is never judged" on a cut that really enters the part held in the stock:
- `engrave_law.rs`: `a_cut_on_the_stock_is_never_judged_by_the_mark_law` -> `a_cut_on_the_stock_answers_to_the_mark_law_against_the_part`; `the_program_sim_credits_the_mark_and_nothing_past_it` now credits the stock-source 0.3 mm mark (0 cells) and charges a 7 mm one 4.0, like the whole model.
- `trochoid_law.rs`: `a_trochoid_on_the_stock_is_never_judged` (#1593's pin, which #1607 asked to keep or restate) -> `a_trochoid_on_the_stock_answers_for_the_part`.
- `circular_pick_law.rs`: `a_circle_picked_off_the_stock_is_never_judged` -> `..._answers_for_the_part`.
- `circular_entity_law.rs`: `a_stock_source_still_cuts_the_typed_circle_unjudged` -> `a_stock_source_circle_through_the_hole_wall_answers_for_the_part`.
- `slot_picks.rs`: `with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before` keeps its "cut as typed" assertions; the slot through the pocket walls is now a gouge.
- `posting.rs` `a_gouging_program_is_refused_by_the_verification_gate` and `stock_sim_document.rs` `faced_doc` (20 mm model): a stock-source Face below the part's top was asserted silent; it is now the op's gouge too. The sim's verdict and the refusal text (led by the sim's clause on the aligned stock) are unchanged.

For #1621:
- `area_controls.rs::a_boundary_offset_on_a_tilted_pocket_is_the_flat_offset_pocket_rotated`: the tilted pocket on "part" was compared with a flat one on "twin" in a world that also holds "tower" standing on the block's top; the tilted +3 offset puts the side-on cutter 3 mm into the tower (15 gouges, now on the op), the flat twin has nothing beside it. The frame-door comparison now runs without the tower; the tower's conviction is asserted.
- `stock_source_verdict.rs` (#1094): Op1 (a Bore on the part) now judges the unmarked casting beside it, as the sim does, so its cached verdict carries those gouges; marking the casting raw stock only takes it out of the set, so the three tests that post or read the gate after marking regenerate first (a new `regenerate` helper; `mark` itself unchanged so the undo/redo tests keep their history).

No golden and no snapshot changes.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on c74d888d (sim 99 s, motion 0 s, app 838 s, ui 19 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean on the same tree. (Earlier: green on e6c0f9c0 before the #1615 merge and #1621.)

## Not exercised
- The 3+2 frame branch with a stock-source op over a part (same code shape as #1603's; `tilt.rs` covers only the no-stock case).
- 2D Chamfer and the hole kinds (Drill, Bore, Thread) on a stock source stay at `None` (not in #1607's list; the chamfer's depth is derived and its break is credited only on the part, the hole kinds would need modelled hole rims excused).
- The sim's mark credit still credits a neighbour part the budget (the op is the stricter judge there): #1627.
- The neighbour law tightens by the source's fidelity excess, not each neighbour's.
- **Staleness (#1628, P1, filed):** the op's stamp digests only its source, so a part moved into a stock-source or part-source op's cut AFTER generation leaves the op Ok; on a turned stock that posts (not a regression: before this branch those parts were not judged at all). A stamp term over the kept set was built and pinned here (f4d86b41, 6abccc77) and taken back out (c74d888d): it re-states "workholding never stales", "a stock-based path never reads the model" and the fidelity refusal on a deleted stock source (5 existing tests) - a maintainer's call; #1628 has the options.
- A stock-source Circular legal-path pin: a Circular in the pocket to its floor carries a pre-existing `RapidInStock` on its diagonal exit rapid (present without this change), so the legal row uses the Slot.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1607-stock-source-law.md` (also corrects #1543's and #1593's "a Stock source cuts unjudged"; the #1615 merge and #1621 sections added).

MCP: no new command or tool; `add_operation` / `generate` / `verify` reach the law (pinned).

Changelog: A 2D Engrave, Trace, Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular, Contour or Face whose source is the stock (or a pick off it) is judged against the parts standing in that stock - a mark law for Engrave and Trace, the solid law for the rest - so a cut into a part is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused even where the program sim cannot judge; a legal mark off the stock now posts on an aligned stock (#1607). A part-source 2D operation is also judged against the setup's other parts with the plain solid law, so a cut on one part that enters a neighbouring part is refused on the operation (#1621).

title: fix(post): Tormach states the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

**`tormach.cps` now states the clearance height before a section's first X/Y traverse.** This applies after a tool change, after a G30, and at the program start. An upright section first writes `G0 Z<clearance>`:
- the clearance is the stream's `PARAM ClearancePlane`, else its `RetractPlane` (the hop, #1028);
- it is never below the move's own Z.

A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, once per program: "first X/Y traverse ... with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) ...". Indexed (4th-axis) sections keep their own order: `indexFor` lifts with G53 and turns A, and their X/Y is the turned tip. The microARC tester-kit program shows the clearance landing right after `G0 A0`.

**Why (from a PathPilot Hub run, 770MX sim v2.14.4).** Hub's T4 was 5" long, and the session's G54 Z zero sat about 4.3" below the top of Z travel. After `G43 H4` the tip stood about 0.68" under the part top, and the bare `G0 X.. Y..` crossed the part at that height. The user saw "down, over, up". #1596 re-lifts with `G53 G0 Z0` after `G43`, which covers a low stored G30. The top of travel itself can still be below clearance when the tool is long for the work offset; that is what this PR covers.
- On a setup that can clear, the new `G0 Z` is an ordinary move down to clearance before the traverse.
- On a setup that cannot, the control refuses that block as past its Z limit and the program stops. It no longer rapids through the part.

`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` states the law.

### Goldens regenerated (WRITE_GOLDEN=1); each gains exactly one `G0 Z..` line before its first X/Y traverse, nothing else
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/`: the 13 legacy programs (`contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole`), plus `index_4face_microarc4`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_bore_centre_mm`, `probe_boss_centre`, `probe_corner`, `probe_edge`, `probe_face` and `probe_guard_moves`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/tormach/`: `contour_plate_with_hole`, `drill_peck`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_tormach.nc`: `G0 Z5` (its ClearancePlane 10 minus OriginZ 5).
- `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/tormach.nc`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/`: `arcs`, `drill_retract`, `extreme_coords`, `full_circle`, `full_circle_raw`, `probe`.
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc`.

That is 32 files, 32 added lines. No snapshot PNG was touched.

### Test inputs given the plane a real section carries
- `tests/common/legacy_program.rs` `as_program` now states `PARAM ClearancePlane` from the legacy golden's `START` height.
- These hand-written streams gain `PARAM ClearancePlane`: `tormach_post.rs`, `tormach_program_end.rs`, `tormach_routers.rs`, `tormach_safe_retract.rs`, `tormach_toolchange_lift.rs`, `tormach_fourth_axis.rs`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle.rs` and the post crate's `work_offset_index.rs`.
- `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up` now asserts the new order: a Z-only `G0 Z0.3937` (the 10 mm clearance), then X/Y alone.

## Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/tormach_traverse_clearance.rs`)

| Test | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first` | the `G0 Z` is removed |
| `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated` | the `G0 Z` is removed, or the RetractPlane fallback is removed |
| `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height` | the `G0 Z` is removed, or the max with the move's own Z is removed |
| `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` | the refusal is removed |

All four mutations were checked; each one fails the test(s) above.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post` (all debug suites) before the input and golden updates: 14 targets failed. All of it was the expected fallout listed above. After the updates every one passes.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites, app suites 885 s, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- **The Hub re-run.** The new `drill_peck` and `contour_plate_with_hole` (inch, 770MX) are in the user's hub-tests folder `1614-770MX/` for that run.
- **The other mill posts.** They have the same pattern and are filed as **#1616** (P1, effort:high, area:post): grblhal and carvera make a bare X/Y traverse; the Fanuc family makes a combined first rapid from the tool-change height.
- The release-lane `--ignored` suites and the UI suites (no UI code touched).

Changelog: The Tormach mill post states the section's clearance Z before its first X/Y traverse after a tool change (and refuses a stream that states no clearance or retract plane), so a tool too long for the work offset stops at the control's Z limit instead of rapiding through the part.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Fixes #1614

title: fix(2d): judge Engrave/Trace as a mark and keep the part under the pocket family, on the operation itself
body:
Fork synced at v0.19.0; branch merged with upstream/main f2b42e3d (#1597 is in it).

Two P1s with one root: a 2D operation at `DepthLaw::None` had no judge of its own, so its verdict rode on the program sim, and the sim refuses a turned stock. Both are fixed with a law the operation carries. `uncovered()` is unchanged (see below).

## #1595 - Engrave and Trace: the mark law
- `DepthLaw::Mark` (`crates/app/src/operation/mark_law.rs`) for both kinds on a finished-part source, whole model or pick. Under the cutter the part's surface may give way by the **mark budget**, `min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`, and no more.
- The test is the existing solid law (`verify::solid_hits`) run against the part lowered by the budget. A cutting move that still enters it is a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on that move, and the path carries a note that names the budget.
- It convicts three things: a cut deeper than a mark, a Top typed below the surface, and a wall standing beside the line (a picked pocket floor is traced along the wall's foot).
- The program sim credits the same mark (`stock_sim::credit_marks` in the sim crate, beside #303's `credit_breaks`; the shared walk is now `edge_break::credit_floors`). A column the mark's own cutter swept is judged against `max(that sweep, model top - budget, underside + 0.2 mm)`. The budget is computed from the operation each time, never read from the cached path, and only an Engrave or Trace on the part declares one.
- **A mark is bounded by the part under the cutter** (review fix, 4f05e9c0). The cutting edge may not come within `MARK_FLOOR` (0.2 mm) of an underside of the part: its bottom, or the roof of a void in it. The operation sweeps the edge against the undersides raised into a solid 0.2 mm high (`verify::seat_skin`); the sim adds `underside + MARK_FLOOR` to its credit floor. So a mark is never deeper than `min(budget, thickness under the cutter - 0.2)`. A deeper cut is a blocking `Gouge` and the path note says "cuts through the part".
- **Only the cutting edge gets the budget** (review fix). The shank and holder on a cutting move, and the whole assembly on a rapid, are judged against the part as it stands (`verify::stack_hits`). One excuse: the straight retract up out of the kerf the cutting move before it made (pinned).

Readings on the #1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, 6 mm end mill), whole-model source, Top 8:

| cut | before: aligned / turned | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.02 mm, 0.3 mm deep | refused by the sim / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| 3.0 mm deep (the radius) | refused by the sim / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| 3.1 mm deep | refused by the sim / posts | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| 7 mm deep (the issue's repro) | refused by the sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Top typed 7 (surface at 8), 0.3 stated | refused by the sim / posts | yes | refused / refused |
| pocket floor picked, 0.3 deep | - | yes | refused / refused |

So before this PR no engraving on a model could post on an aligned stock (0.02 mm included), and any depth posted on a turned one.

Readings on the review's thin plate (40 x 40 x 2, 6 mm end mill, whole-model source, Top 2; Engrave and Trace alike):

| cut | op | aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|
| Bottom -0.9 (through the plate; budget 2.9) | Gouge, "cuts through the part" | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| 1.9 mm deep (0.1 mm of plate left) | Gouge, "cuts through the part" | refused (sim charges 0.10) / refused |
| 1.8 mm deep (exactly 0.2 mm left) | 0 | posts / posts |
| 0.3 mm deep | 0 | posts / posts |
| 8 mm block, 2.5 mm deep with 2 mm of flute (shank 0.5 mm in the part) | ShankHit on the part | refused / refused |

At 976cda6c the first row posted on both stocks with no finding (M5's reproduction in pullrequestreview-5900983707).

Re-checked on `Milling-test.step` (EM-0600, whole model, both stocks): Engrave and Trace post at 0.3 mm and at exactly 3.0 mm and are refused at 3.2 mm (the sim charges 0.20 mm); a default whole-model Pocket (stock top to Z10) posts on both stocks. The three changed fixtures are untouched by the review fix.

## #1603 - the pocket family: the keep law
- `DepthLaw::Keep` (`crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`) for 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset on a whole-model source: the solid law alone, against the source's mesh. It applies where the pocket clears the stock around the part (#12). With no stock set up the model is still the volume to remove, and the law stands down (`GenJob::around_part`).
- On a **stock source** (or a pick off the stock) the same law runs against the setup's parts (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`, the mesh the program sim judges against), carried in the job as `keep_parts`. A setup with no part judges nothing.

Readings on the #12 fixture (30 x 30 x 10 block, 12 x 12 boss to Z20, 10 mm end mill, 50 x 50 x 20 stock), cut to Z5:

| case | before: op gouges, turned stock | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| whole model, Area offset +3 (Pocket, Adaptive) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| whole model, extension +5 (Pocket, Adaptive) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| stock source (Pocket, Adaptive; #1554's cut) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| whole model, default controls (Pocket, Adaptive, Offset) | 0, posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| stock source stopping on the part's top | 0, posts | 0 | posts / posts |

## `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs): not changed
Both issues asked whether a None-law op on a model source should stop counting as judged when the sim cannot judge. It was measured against its own test and declined:
- it would refuse every legal whole-model Pocket, Adaptive and Offset on a turned stock (they were at `None`), which is a false refusal;
- it keeps the verdict tied to whether the sim can model the stock;
- it cannot name the move.

With `Mark` and `Keep`, the only 2D kind still at `None` on a model source is the 2D Chamfer (derived depth, credited by #303). The legal rows above post on a turned stock, pinned.

## Existing tests that changed
Three fixtures ran a stock-source pocket straight through a part and asserted a silent verify. Each is a real cut into the part, which #1603 asks to be refused:
- `post_not_judged.rs`, `machine_switch.rs` (the tilted pocket): the part filled the whole stock. The part is now the 10 mm the pocket leaves, so the cut stops on it. The assertions are unchanged.
- `lead_approach.rs` (two tests on the user's stock-source pocket on `Milling-test.step`): they now assert the gouge on the user's part and read the entry laws on the remaining warnings.
- `authored_law_tests.rs`: #1593's audit table is split into `the_2d_chamfer_alone_stays_unjudged_on_the_part`, `the_pocket_family_keeps_a_whole_model_and_sections_a_pick` and `engrave_and_trace_on_the_part_answer_to_the_mark_law`.

No golden and no snapshot changes. `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens` pass unchanged.

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/engrave_law.rs` (9; generate, then post, on both stocks; Engrave and Trace):
- `a_whole_model_cut_deep_under_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`
- `a_shallow_mark_is_clean_on_the_operation_and_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `the_mark_budget_ends_at_the_cutter_radius_on_both_stocks_alike`
- `a_top_typed_under_the_surface_is_not_a_mark`
- `a_picked_floor_traced_along_its_wall_gouges_the_wall_and_never_posts`
- `a_picked_top_face_marked_shallow_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `a_cut_on_the_stock_is_never_judged_by_the_mark_law`
- `the_program_sim_credits_the_mark_and_nothing_past_it`
- `over_mcp_a_whole_model_engrave_and_trace_are_judged_the_same` (MCP `add_operation`, `verify`)

`crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs` (7; Pocket and Adaptive, both stocks):
- `a_whole_model_area_offset_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_whole_model_extension_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_stock_source_cut_through_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_legal_whole_model_clearing_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks` (Pocket, Adaptive, Offset)
- `a_stock_source_cut_that_stops_on_the_part_stays_clean_and_posts`
- `a_stock_source_cut_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `over_mcp_the_pocket_family_keeps_the_part_the_same` (MCP `add_operation`, `set_operation_area`, `verify`)

`crates/app/tests/mark_floor.rs` (4, the review fix; generate, then post, on both stocks; Engrave and Trace):
- `a_cut_through_a_thin_plate_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`
- `a_mark_that_leaves_the_floor_posts_on_both_stocks_and_one_that_does_not_is_refused`
- `the_program_sim_never_credits_a_cut_through_the_plate` (the sim's own verdict, aligned)
- `a_shank_in_the_kerf_is_judged_against_the_part_as_it_stands`

`crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs` (9; new: `a_budget_deeper_than_the_plate_never_credits_a_cut_through_it`, `a_mark_on_a_thin_plate_is_credited_down_to_the_floor_it_must_leave`, `a_mark_over_a_void_is_credited_only_down_to_the_roof_it_must_leave`), the unit tests in `mark_law_tests.rs` (13; new: the part under the cutter, a void's roof, the shank, the rapid, the kerf retract, the two notes), `crates/sim/src/verify/seat.rs` (5: undersides whatever the winding, a face between two bodies, a void's roof, the skin, an unreadable mesh) and `authored_law_tests.rs`.

Both fixtures place the box stock centred over the part and assert its bounds.

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | result |
