title: fix(contour)!: climb milling runs climb - outside clockwise, inside counter-clockwise with M3
body:
**Breaking (post output):** every 2D Contour and 2D Chamfer posted from an existing project changes direction, and G41/G42 swap under control or wear compensation. A project that set `climb: false` to get climb milling now posts conventional. That is why the title is `fix!`. The release notes must say so.

Branched from upstream `main` d00243a5 (fork synced at v0.19.0).

## What changed

With a right-hand spindle (M3, clockwise seen from +Z), climb milling keeps the material on the **right** of the tool's travel. So an outside profile runs **clockwise**, an inside profile (a hole wall) **counter-clockwise**, and control compensation is **G41**. Conventional is the reverse of all three. Source: Machinery's Handbook ("Milling Practice", climb vs conventional milling) for the direction, and RS-274 / ISO 6983 for G41 (cutter left of the contour along the direction of travel). Every 2D mill op posts M3; only thread milling can ask for M4, and it has its own hand law. Adaptive, Bore and Circular already work this way and also don't read the spindle. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1555-climb-direction.md`.

I found the cause where the issue said: `contour.rs` treated "material on the left" as climb. I checked every user of the direction rule and the climb flag:

| Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `machining2d::contour`: outside/inside ring travel | `climb != inside` walked stored (material left) | `climb == inside` walks stored, via `ring::walked` |
| `contour::air_side`: leads, `lead_fit`, `contour_entry`, `contour_chain` | climb meant air on the right | climb means air on the left |
| `Legal::air_left` (fillets, lead room) | `!climb` | `climb` |
| `contour_comp::side_of` (control and wear compensation) | climb = G42 | climb = **G41**, conventional = G42 |
| `contour_comp_room::arcs` (inside-arc room law) | took the tool side from the contour side, which was only right in 1 of 4 cases | takes it from the travel (climb = left) |
| `arc_leads` (comments only) | | sign words updated; the math follows `air_side` |
| `app::operation::contour_open` (contour on an open boundary) | run order was the chain's lexicographic order, unrelated to the side | run handed on with the material on its right |
| `machining2d::chamfer` + app `Chamfer2D` | climb walked stored order (material left on a boss edge) | new `ChamferParams::inside` (from Side): boss edge CW, bore edge CCW under climb |
| 2D Pocket wall pass (Waterline / Offset rings / Adaptive, `waterscan`, `adaptive/wall`) | already CCW under climb | **unchanged**, pinned. The issue's pocket row did not reproduce on main with any strategy (motion disc and app block-with-hole) |
| Zigzag pocket rows, Face rows, Slot rows | serpentine: half the rows are climb whatever the flag | unchanged (the flag only picks the first row) |
| Trace, open centerline contour run | on the line: material on both sides or none | travel unchanged; a centerline run's lead now leaves to the other side (both sides are air as far as the run knows) |
| Deburr | has no climb parameter | unchanged |

Three changes came out of the flip:
- **Seams stay put** (`ring::walked`). Each ring keeps the seam the old default had: the outside ring's first point, the inside ring's last point (the axis-aligned point on a tessellated bore). Climb and conventional now differ only in direction. Without this, the climb bore started on a 0.7-degree facet: its arc entry became an oblique chord fan and the verify flagged `RapidInStock` (`one_descent`).
- **Keep-down ring-to-ring links** are now also checked against both rings' leads. Under climb, the straight link between two bosses crosses the next boss's lead-out arc (verify `Crossing`). It now lifts at that spot, with a note ("staying down would have crossed passes"), instead of posting a crossing that the gate would block.
- **`cl::PathBuilder::push_arc_in`** no longer splits a vertical arc at a Z extremum that sits at the arc's off-lattice end. That split left a 0.2 um sliver arc on the climb bore's arc entry (`arc_entry::the_arc_entry_changes_only_the_descents`).

## Goldens: direction reversed, same geometry, same seam

Regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`, and only the suites that failed. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- CL: `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole_blended`, `contour_disc_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `contour_start_point`, `contour_bore_arc_entry`. Outside rings now run clockwise and hole rings counter-clockwise; leads mirror to the air side.
- NC (each dialect's copy of those programs: fanuc, carvera, doosan-dnm, grblhal, haas, heidenhain, mazak, sinumerik, tinyg, tormach, plus the inch set of `contour_plate_with_hole`): G2 and G3 swap on the walls and on the arc leads.
- NC compensation: `contour_control_comp` and `contour_wear_comp` (fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik). G42 becomes **G41** (climb outside, M3), and `COMP RIGHT` becomes `COMP LEFT`.
- NC `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form`: its roughing contour round the boss now runs G02 (clockwise).
- Post recorded inputs `vertical_arc_{x,y,oblique}.cl`: the inside ring now runs counter-clockwise. The post's `vertical_arc_entry` checks still hold (G18/G19 arcs, chords for oblique).

## Pins and mutation checks

New pins: `crates/motion/tests/climb_direction.rs` (9 tests), `crates/app/tests/climb_direction.rs` (2 tests, through `operation::generate` with the verify), and `area_open::the_open_pass_runs_climb_with_the_material_on_its_right`. Corrected pins (each still asserts something, none deleted): `contour_inside_shrinks_and_flips_travel` (now CCW), `conventional_inside_travels_reversed` (renamed from `..._forward`; now CW), `machining2d::climb_and_conventional_reverse_the_travel`, `control_comp` / `wear_comp` sides (motion and app; two app fns renamed `..._under_g41_...`). `level_links::contour_ring_to_ring_keep_down_is_proved_or_named` keeps its stay-down cases on conventional and adds the climb case (lifts, named, verify clean). `law_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` (ui) now runs on the conventional walk; see "Not exercised".

What each pin checks, from `climb_direction`:
- Outside contour, climb + M3, runs CW (signed sweep < 0); conventional runs CCW. `climb_outside_contour_runs_clockwise_and_conventional_counter_clockwise`
- Inside contour and round hole wall, climb, run CCW. `climb_inside_contour_...`, `climb_hole_wall_contour_runs_counter_clockwise`
- 2D Pocket wall pass, climb = CCW and conventional = CW, for Waterline, Offset rings, Adaptive and Auto. `pocket_wall_pass_climb_runs_counter_clockwise` (motion), `the_2d_pocket_wall_pass_runs_counter_clockwise_under_climb` (app: block with a 20 x 20 blind hole, Waterline / Offset rings / Adaptive, verify silent, analytic-solid gouge check)
- With control compensation, climb gives G41 and conventional G42, on both sides, and the centre walks the matching direction. `control_compensation_posts_g41_for_climb_and_g42_for_conventional`, plus the posted NC goldens above
- Leads stay on the air side (outside: centre at least 3 mm off the part; inside: within the bore's centre area) and arc leads stay tangent at the join after the flip, for both travels. `leads_stay_on_the_air_side_after_the_flip`, `arc_leads_stay_tangent_after_the_flip`
- Sim / verify: `the_2d_contour_runs_clockwise_outside_and_counter_clockwise_in_the_hole_under_climb` generates outside and hole contours on the block with a hole, with leads None / Arc / Tangential / Perpendicular and both travels. Each gets `operation::generate`'s verify (no warnings) and an analytic-solid gouge scan (no point of the cutter inside the block).
- Chamfer: boss edge CW and bore edge CCW under climb. `chamfer_climb_keeps_the_material_right`

Mutation results. For each, I re-inverted one rule, confirmed red, and restored with `git checkout` (tree clean after):

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| M1: ring rule `climb == inside` changed to `!=` | climb_outside..., climb_inside..., climb_hole_wall..., control_compensation..., arc_leads_stay_tangent... |
| M2: `air_side` climb branch put back to air-right | control_compensation..., arc_leads_stay_tangent... |
| M3: `side_of` swapped back (climb = G42) | control_compensation_posts_g41... |
| M4: chamfer rule inverted | chamfer_climb_keeps_the_material_right |
| M5: waterline pocket ring order inverted (shows the pocket pin bites) | pocket_wall_pass_climb_runs_counter_clockwise |
| M6: open-boundary run reversal removed | the_open_pass_runs_climb_with_the_material_on_its_right |
| M7: ring rule inverted, app level | the_2d_contour_runs_clockwise_outside_and_counter_clockwise_in_the_hole_under_climb |
| M8: keep-down link proof without the leads | contour_ring_to_ring_keep_down_is_proved_or_named |

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on 0adc69d3+6a40091e. It fell back to batch size because `cl` was touched. geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion suites passed, and so did `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates. App was red only on `thread_boss` (a stale NC golden, regenerated in 86f73eba, now green). UI was red only on `law_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` (see below; the ui lib is now 731/731 green). The earlier targeted runs of app `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`, `verify`, `operations`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `wall_arc_entry`, `lead_approach`, `arc_entry`, `contour_start_point`, `conformance`, `program_units`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle`, `per_op_files`, `cli`, `corner_blend` and `area_open`, plus the whole post crate, were all green after the golden regeneration.

## Not exercised / follow-ups

- The repro in the issue (the user's end-cap plate over MCP and the Tormach post) was not re-run through the CLI. The same law is pinned through `operation::generate` and the posted NC goldens.
- `ui::law_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` now runs on the conventional walk. At its coarse 0.1 mm tolerance on a tessellated Ø30 cylinder stock, the climb walk's arc fit sits about 0.01 mm past the wall. The verify flags it as a gouge (so the post is held, not silent), and the overlay draws it red instead of green. The arc fitter's split points depend on the walk direction, and this fixture lands on the wrong side of the 0.01 mm gouge tolerance. I'm filing it as a follow-up issue.
- M4 spindle for mill ops: not supported today (only thread milling reverses), so it is not read. The decision file says what has to flip if that ever changes.
- 2D Chamfer `Side::Auto` is treated as a boss edge (material inside the picked loops). A bore edge needs `Side: Inside` to climb counter-clockwise.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: 2D Contour and 2D Chamfer climb milling now runs climb with the M3 spindle - outside profiles clockwise, inside profiles counter-clockwise, G41 under control/wear compensation (BREAKING: posted direction reverses; projects that set climb off as a workaround now post conventional) (#1555)

Fixes #1555

title: fix(import): refuse a STEP closed shell that meshes open, by name
body:
## What changed
- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_closed.rs` finds the shells the file declares closed (`CLOSED_SHELL`, and the outer shell a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` names) and judges each one's kept mesh (`judge`).
- `step_facets.rs` (new): each tessellation pass keeps every face's mesh apart, oriented as truck's `to_polygon` would, and records the facet range each face owns. `step.rs` uses it in place of `to_polygon`.
- `step_seams.rs` (new): the seams of a closed shell, vertices welded within 1e-6 of the file unit, sorted into three faults:
  - **Reversed face** (a shared edge used twice in the same direction): fixed, not refused. Each face is flipped to agree with its neighbours (exact shared edges, and T-junction sides that run parallel, vote), and each connected group is turned to enclose a positive volume. Logged as a warning naming the face.
  - **T-junction** (neighbouring faces split their shared boundary differently): closed when every boundary edge's ends and midpoint lie within 2 chord tolerances of another face's boundary. Logged.
  - **Gap** (a boundary edge farther than that from every other face): refused. `closed shell #id (N faces) meshes open: K boundary edges lie more than G mm from any other face, most on face #F (i of N), up to W mm; the first from (..) to (..) mm[; face #D got no mesh from the kernel]`.
- A face the kernel returns no mesh for is still refused by name in any shell. Open shells keep the kernel's winding and are not seam-checked.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/1573-closed-shell-watertight.md`, including the Prime-Directive call on the two corpus files (below).

## How tested
- Unit tests (`step_seams`, synthetic cube meshed face by face): `a_face_wound_against_its_neighbours_is_flipped_not_called_open`, `the_flips_turn_the_shell_outward`, `a_boundary_split_differently_on_each_side_is_closed`, `a_reversed_face_met_only_through_t_junctions_is_still_flipped`, `a_boundary_bowed_within_the_gap_tolerance_is_closed`, `a_real_gap_wider_than_the_tolerance_is_found`, `a_missing_face_leaves_a_gap`, `a_face_never_closes_its_own_boundary`, `copies_of_a_vertex_within_the_weld_still_meet`, `the_importer_closes_seams_within_two_chord_tolerances_only`.
- `crates/app/tests/import_step_closed_shell.rs`: `a_closed_shell_that_meshes_open_is_refused_by_name` (bent fillet_corner), `a_face_the_kernel_cannot_mesh_is_refused_in_an_open_shell_too`, `the_outer_shell_of_a_solid_is_closed_whatever_its_keyword` (pins the MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP read), `a_face_wound_against_its_neighbours_imports_flipped_not_refused` (box.step with one face's `same_sense` and bound flipped: imports with the same facet count and the same signed volume as the original), `every_solid_step_fixture_still_imports`.

title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.
- `motion` unit test `the_cone_rule_holds_the_lean_and_refuses_a_lead_into_a_corner`; `post` unit test `taper_angle_words_parse_and_garbled_ones_refuse_the_file`.
- U/V goldens: `wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_verify` pass with their goldens unedited.
- Merge-time refresh (merge of upstream main df90b031, head 9673a77e): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 21.1 min; 3215 tests passed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; golden `wire_taper_angle_punch.nc` unchanged.
- Gate on the pre-refresh head 39d014d8: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/537-wire-4axis` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 11.2 min); the wire suites by hand (wire_taper 5, wire_4axis 6, wire_post 5, wire_contour 7, wire_verify 3, wire_taper_angle 4: all pass); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10). The angle code and dialect words are invented on the synthetic fixture.
- How a real control ramps the lean over the lead-in and lead-out is modelled as a linear ramp, the same as #536. The decision record states this.

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

## How tested
- motion `turning_thread_infeed`, 10/10, including two new tests:
  - every roughing depth is cut twice (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.2) and the default is unchanged move for move;
  - a repeat is the same pass under every method × schedule, and the verdict stays silent.
- app:
  - `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5: the toggle goes stale and back to OK, takes 3 then 5 plunges, with undo and redo; round-trip writes the key only when set;
  - `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 5/5: G76 refuses the repeat; `REP 1` rides the stream; G32 posts 5 passes.
- `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `inverted_post`, `project_roundtrip` and the app lib pass. No golden changed.
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on cl, post, motion, app and ui is clean.
- The only failure is the headless-GPU ui test (no adapter on this Mac).

## Not exercised (draft)
GUI check and a lathe sim or machine run. There is a combined test kit for #416, #417 and #418.

Changelog: Threading op: optional repeat of each roughing depth (G32 output; G76 refuses it by name) (#418)

Fixes #418

Before is upstream/main, so the after-shot also shows the stacked parents' rows (#516 infeed plan). After: the same plan as #516's after-shot (Flank 29.5°, Constant area, minimum depth 0.05 mm, finish allowance 0.03 mm, 1 spring pass) with **Repeat each depth** on - the new row this PR adds.

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

**R comes from the rounded words' own ladder (M3 review fix, head 0bb37ddd).** The control reads the posted words, each rounded to the least increment on its own. In inch, `Q157 P472 R0.0157` left k − d = 0.0315 one increment past the second rung 0.0314, so the control cut a 4th, unverified pass. Now the post counts the record's rough passes N from its own ladder, rebuilds rungs N−1 and N from the rounded Q (first depth), Q (minimum depth) and P (thread height), and writes the R whose last rough depth P − R lies in (rung N−1, rung N], nearest the record's allowance. Inch golden: `R0.0157` → `R0.0158` (control: 0.0157 / 0.0314 / 0.0472). If that R is more than one least increment from the record's allowance, the cycle is refused by name (the Q/Q/P words and the R window are named). The other G76 words (X, Z, P k, Q dd, Q dmin) are each one record value rounded once, not differences, so R was the only derived word. The Tormach (LinuxCNC) G76 has the same class of gap in J/K (inch `J0.0314 K0.0944` = ceil 4 passes for a 3-pass record), filed as #1619. Its goldens are left byte-identical to main here.

**A project cached before this fix posts R0 until the op is regenerated.** Checked: the stale stamp (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`, `current_stamp`) hashes only the operation's inputs (tool, params, source, heights). It has no generator version, and the cached record's `finish_allowance` reads back as saved. So such an op reads **Fresh**, not Stale, and posts the old `R0` schedule (one extra root pass, mm) until it is regenerated. The stale-stamp machinery does not catch it today.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- M3 review fix (head 0bb37ddd), two new tests in `lathe_post_g76_schedule`:
  - `the_default_thread_g76_states_its_three_passes_in_inch`: posts the default thread under G20, parses the G76 words, runs the control's ladder on them, and asserts exactly 3 passes matching the laid depths (`R0.0158`).
  - `a_ladder_the_rounded_words_cannot_state_is_refused_by_name`: two hand-edited inch records (13 and 39 sqrt rungs, 2 and 4 increments off) are refused by name, and the same record in mm posts.
  - Mutations, each red and then reverted: R back to `fu(finish)` (inch twin + refusal test); refusal dropped (refusal test); check `> 2` (refusal test, 2-increment case); check `> 0` / `>= 1` (inch twin + refusal test).
  - Gate: app lathe_post_g76 8, lathe_post_g76_schedule 6, lathe_post_inch 6, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_tormach 8, lathe_post_tormach_thread 8, tormach_lathes 2, recorded_post_streams 5; post lathe_post_refusals 11, script_fanuc_lathe 15; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean. Tormach lathe goldens: `git diff upstream/main` empty.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- Takeover refresh at 49d0a3c2: merged upstream/main cleanly, inch golden updated to `R0.0157`; `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (escalated to batch) green with 0 failed, incl. clippy -D warnings.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (no Hub run needed for the merge)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Rounding of the words: handled now (R from the rounded ladder, refused beyond one increment); individual rungs of a long sqrt ladder can still differ from the laid ones by a few increments, with the same pass count.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

Hub run: not needed. The Tormach lathe goldens are byte-identical to main (checked against upstream/main); only Fanuc-lathe goldens change (`thread_g76.nc` mm and inch, new `thread_g76_area.nc`). The inch Fanuc golden now reads `R0.0158`.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417
